title: GTA 6 Made $3.79 Billion in ONE Day — The Insane 13-Year Story
notes: Facts checked 2026-11-23. Sources: Take-Two IR release (Nov 20 2026), Rockstar delay announcements (May 2 2025, Nov 6 2025), BBC/court reporting on the 2022 leak. Budget is NOT disclosed by Rockstar: always say 'estimated'.

segments.text: On November nineteenth, twenty twenty-six... a video game made three point seven nine billion dollars.
shots: stickman businessman in suit staring in shock at a giant glowing pile of gold coins and cash stacks reaching the ceiling, dramatic spotlight

segments.text: In one single day.
shots: close-up of a stickman with jaw dropped and eyes wide, money raining down around him, bright yellow background

segments.text: That's more than Avengers: Endgame made in its entire run in theaters.
shots: empty movie theater with red seats, stickman in popcorn hat looking sad next to a small pile of coins, while a huge mountain of gold glows through the doorway

segments.text: But the story of how Grand Theft Auto Six got here... is wilder than anything in the game.
shots: neon lit tropical city skyline at sunset with palm trees, pink and purple sky, stickman wearing sunglasses on a rooftop looking at the view

segments.text: It involves a teenage hacker in a hotel room,
shots: stickman teenager in a hoodie typing on a phone in a dim hotel room, glowing hotel TV, green code reflections, night

segments.text: a trailer that broke the internet,
shots: giant smartphone screen exploding with likes and hearts, crowd of stickmen holding phones up in amazement, confetti

segments.text: two delays...
shots: stickman gamer collapsing in despair in front of a wall calendar with crossed out dates, dark gloomy bedroom

segments.text: and thirteen years of waiting. Let's get into it.
shots: old stickman with long grey beard sitting on a couch holding a game controller, covered in cobwebs, dusty living room, clock on wall

segments.text: To understand GTA Six, you have to go back to twenty thirteen.
shots: retro living room from 2013 with a boxy flatscreen TV and game console, stickman sitting on the carpet excited, warm lamp light

segments.text: That's when GTA Five came out. And it didn't just sell well...
shots: long line of excited stickmen waiting outside a game store at midnight, neon store sign glow, night street

segments.text: it made eight hundred million dollars on day one, and a billion in three days.
shots: stickman in suit riding a rocket made of money upward through the clouds, celebratory sky

segments.text: Over the next decade, it sold more than two hundred million copies.
shots: huge warehouse filled with endless stacks of game boxes, tiny stickman worker with clipboard looking up in awe

segments.text: Then there was GTA Online. Players kept buying in-game cash... year after year after year.
shots: stickman sitting at a desk buying with a credit card, cartoon money flying out of the computer screen, late night room

segments.text: Which created a strange problem.
shots: stickman executive in an office scratching his head looking at a chart that keeps going up, thinking bubble with question mark

segments.text: Rockstar was making so much money from an old game... there was no rush to make a new one.
shots: stickman boss relaxing in a hammock between two palm trees on a beach, holding a coconut drink, piles of money nearby

segments.text: Behind the scenes, though, work had started.
shots: huge open plan game studio office at night, rows of stickmen developers at glowing computer screens, focused

segments.text: Early planning reportedly began around twenty fifteen.
shots: stickman designers around a table covered in maps, sketches and sticky notes, whiteboard with city drawing

segments.text: And after Red Dead Redemption Two shipped in twenty eighteen, most of the studio moved onto the next big thing.
shots: stickman cowboy hanging his hat on a hook and walking toward a door that opens onto a bright neon city, symbolic transition

segments.text: Developers even flew to Miami to study the city up close.
shots: stickmen tourists with cameras and notebooks on a Miami beach boardwalk, art deco hotels, palm trees, bright sunny day

segments.text: Meanwhile, fans were losing their minds.
shots: crowd of angry stickmen gamers holding blank protest signs outside a building, comedic angry faces

segments.text: Every year, someone predicted the announcement.
shots: stickman conspiracy theorist in front of a cork board covered in photos connected with red string, intense eyes

segments.text: Every year, it didn't happen.
shots: sad stickman alone at a party with deflated balloons and a cake, empty room, gloomy blue light

segments.text: Waiting for GTA Six became a joke on its own.
shots: skeleton stickman sitting in a gaming chair still holding a controller, dusty room, spider webs, comedic

segments.text: Then, in September twenty twenty-two... everything changed.
shots: dark computer screen glowing red with a warning symbol, stickman developer jumping back in shock, dramatic red lighting

segments.text: Ninety clips of early, unfinished GTA Six footage appeared online.
shots: dozens of floating video screens with blurry unfinished game footage swirling in a dark space, stickman staring at them

segments.text: Rough animations. Debug text. Unfinished buildings. Seen by millions.
shots: unfinished grey blocky city made of plain boxes, a stickman character in a T-pose standing in the middle, glitchy

segments.text: Rockstar confirmed it. They had been hacked.
shots: serious stickman executive at a press podium with microphones, camera flashes, dark blue background

segments.text: But the most shocking part was who did it.
shots: shadowy silhouette of a hooded stickman figure in a doorway, single spotlight, mystery mood

segments.text: Police say it was a teenager from England, part of a hacking group called Lapsus.
shots: stickman teenager in a hoodie surrounded by floating holographic padlocks breaking open, dark blue cyber room

segments.text: And he pulled it off while on bail... from a hotel room.
shots: small budget hotel room at night, single bed, stickman in hoodie sitting cross legged with a phone, curtains drawn

segments.text: Police had already taken his laptop. So he reportedly used an Amazon Fire Stick, the hotel TV, and his phone.
shots: close-up of a hotel TV with a small streaming stick plugged in, phone on the bed, glowing screen in a dark room

segments.text: In twenty twenty-three, a court ordered him to be held in a secure hospital indefinitely.
shots: stickman judge with white wig in a wooden courtroom raising a gavel, serious mood, warm wood tones

segments.text: Rockstar said it was extremely disappointed... but development would continue.
shots: determined stickman developers rolling up their sleeves at their desks, sunrise light through office windows

segments.text: The leaks weren't over.
shots: water dripping from a cracked pipe labeled with nothing, stickman plumber looking worried with a bucket

segments.text: In December twenty twenty-three, the first official trailer leaked a day early.
shots: stickman sneaking out of a building carrying a glowing film reel, night alley, comedic spy pose

segments.text: So Rockstar just... released it.
shots: stickman pressing a huge red button labeled with nothing, shrugging, comedic office scene

segments.text: Ninety million views on YouTube in twenty-four hours. A record.
shots: view counter odometer spinning wildly with smoke coming out, stickmen cheering around it, confetti and fireworks

segments.text: We were going back to Vice City... Rockstar's take on Miami.
shots: neon pink and teal tropical city at night, art deco hotels, palm trees, sports car driving along the beach road

segments.text: Set in Leonida. A fictional version of Florida.
shots: sunny swamp with alligators and airboats, a stickman in shorts waving from the boat, Florida everglades

segments.text: Complete with alligators, swamps... and the kind of chaos you'd see in a viral Florida Man headline.
shots: stickman man in flip flops riding an alligator through a convenience store parking lot, chaotic comedic, sunny day

segments.text: And for the first time in the modern series... a female lead. Lucia.
shots: confident stickman woman with ponytail in a leather jacket standing in front of a neon city at night, heroic pose

segments.text: Alongside her partner Jason, in a story inspired by Bonnie and Clyde.
shots: stickman couple running away from a bank holding bags of money, police lights in the background, night street, dramatic

segments.text: The plan was a twenty twenty-five release. Fans counted down.
shots: excited stickmen crossing days off a giant calendar with markers, party hats, bright room

segments.text: Then, in May twenty twenty-five... delayed. To May twenty twenty-six.
shots: stickman knocking over a calendar in frustration, papers flying, dramatic grey office

segments.text: Days later, trailer two dropped... and Rockstar said it hit four hundred and seventy-five million views across platforms in its first day.
shots: huge stadium crowd of stickmen watching a giant screen, lights and lasers, ecstatic faces

segments.text: Then, in November twenty twenty-five... delayed again. To November nineteenth, twenty twenty-six.
shots: stickman lying face down on the floor next to a controller, dark rain outside the window, comedic despair

segments.text: Rockstar said it needed the time to deliver the polish players expect.
shots: stickman craftsman carefully polishing a shiny golden trophy with a cloth, workshop, warm light

segments.text: Nobody outside the company knows the real budget. But estimates run from one to two billion dollars... or more.
shots: stickman accountant with glasses surrounded by towering stacks of papers and a long receipt unrolling across the floor

segments.text: And then... November nineteenth finally arrived.
shots: city street at midnight packed with stickmen celebrating, fireworks in the sky, neon lights everywhere

segments.text: Before launch, the game had already sold thirty-two and a half million copies.
shots: delivery trucks lined up outside a giant warehouse, stickmen loading boxes, busy night scene

segments.text: By the end of day one... three point seven nine billion dollars.
shots: stickman in suit swimming in a vault full of gold coins, joyful, sparkles

segments.text: Take-Two called it the biggest launch in entertainment history.
shots: stickman holding a giant golden trophy on a stage, spotlights and confetti, cheering audience

segments.text: For comparison, GTA Five made around eight hundred million on its first day.
shots: two stacks of coins side by side, one small and one enormous towering into the clouds, stickman pointing at them

segments.text: That's nearly five times bigger.
shots: stickman measuring a gigantic tower of money with a tiny measuring tape, comedic scale, blue sky

segments.text: So what's the lesson from thirteen years of waiting?
shots: stickman sitting on a hill at sunset looking at a city in the distance, thoughtful, warm orange sky

segments.text: Rockstar ignored the deadlines, the memes... and even a massive leak.
shots: stickman walking calmly through a storm of flying newspapers and paper airplanes, unbothered, umbrella

segments.text: They bet that people would wait for something great.
shots: long line of patient stickmen stretching to the horizon waiting outside a glowing door, golden light

segments.text: And three point seven nine billion dollars later... it looks like they were right.
shots: stickman developer team celebrating on a rooftop at night with the neon city behind them, fireworks

segments.text: So, was it worth the wait? Tell me in the comments.
shots: stickman sitting on a couch playing a video game with a huge smile, cozy living room at night, TV glow

segments.text: And if you like stories like this, subscribe. There's a lot more coming.
shots: friendly stickman waving goodbye in front of a colorful neon city skyline, cheerful
